Areas to define commercial zones. Since they are devised on a county-wide basis, it is asserted that they are too large and include economically unrelated areas. Inequities would also arise between the commercial zones of cities in western States, where counties are generally large, and cities in the eastern States, where counties are smaller. It is also argued that since the SMSA concept is not under Commission control, its utilization would amount to an abdication of our responsibility to administer the Interstate Commerce Act.
Position of the Short Haul Survival Committee. - The Short Haul Survival Committee, an ad hoc committee formed in specific response to the proposed expansion of commercial zone and terminal area limits, is composed of the Local & Short Haul Carriers Conference of the American Trucking Associations, Inc., and 252 individual motor carrier members holding authority from this Commission. The Committee has submitted an extensive brief entitled "Statement of the Short Haul Survival Committee and 252 Individual Motor Carriers in Opposition to the Interim Report of the Commission" (hereinafter referred to as Short Haul Committee or Committee), consisting of legal arguments and economic data. Since this is the most comprehensive representation submitted by opponents of the proposed rules, we believe a separate synopsis of the Committee's position is appropriate.
